title: Segregation, conflicts and disclosures
objectives: Apply the rule separating advice from distribution.
State the disclosures to give a client.
body_md:
The central rule: **advice and distribution must be separate.**

## Segregation

- An **individual IA** must not offer distribution or execution services to **their advisory clients**.
- A **family member or associate** of the IA must not distribute products to those clients either.
- A **non-individual IA** must keep advisory and distribution in **separate** business units, with separate premises, records and personnel.
- An IA cannot receive any consideration from a product provider for advice to the client.

## Client agreement and disclosures

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Services and fees | What is advised, how much, how paid |
| Conflicts | Any interests that might bias the advice |
| Risks | Market risk, no guaranteed returns |
| Grievance | Complaint route: IA, then SEBI SCORES, then Smart ODR |
| Terms | Duration, termination, refund |

## Execute through Direct plans

When advising on mutual funds, an IA should recommend **Direct plans** (no distributor commission).

> **Exam tip:** If a question mixes advice and commission, the answer is almost always "not allowed".
example: An IA's spouse is an MF distributor. The IA must not route advisory clients to the spouse for execution.
say: I recommend Direct plans so no commission is paid on your investments.
Here are my conflicts, if any, in writing.
never: My brother sells these funds, buy through him.
Our advisory and distribution desks share one team.
